prompts.prompt: Choose one ingredient you both already have and make two different snacks with it while you talk.
Take a ten-minute neighborhood walk on the call and show each other one detail you normally overlook.
Open a blank page, design an imaginary tiny home together, and explain where every object belongs.
Pick three songs each, trade the mini playlists, and share the memory behind one surprising choice.
Make hot drinks, dim the lights, and tell the story of the most peaceful place you remember.
Choose a simple household object and take turns inventing five ridiculous alternative uses for it.
Bring one old photo each, describe what happened outside the frame, and ask one gentle follow-up.
Set a fifteen-minute timer and sketch the view from your windows, then reveal both drawings together.
Plan an imaginary day in a city neither of you has visited using only places you would genuinely enjoy.
Wear one color you both choose, prepare a small treat, and turn an ordinary call into a themed café date.
Each person finds a five-minute tutorial for a harmless skill, then teach the skill to each other on camera.
Build separate blanket forts or cozy corners and hold the rest of the call from your new spaces.
Choose a shared question, record one-minute voice answers privately, then play them at the same time.
Take turns giving a virtual tour of one drawer, shelf, or collection and explain why three items stayed.
Invent a two-person award show with categories such as best shared meal, funniest mistake, and kindest moment.
Select a short public-domain story or poem, read alternating sections aloud, and discuss one favorite line.
Create matching paper airplanes, decorate them with future wishes, and test whose flight lasts longer.
Order no food: use what you have to plate the most restaurant-looking meal or snack, then reveal it.
Choose a season and build a five-item date-night list you can use when you are in the same place again.
Play a camera scavenger race to find something soft, something old, something useful, and something joyful.
Watch the sky from both locations for ten quiet minutes, then compare the colors, sounds, and weather.
Write six words that describe your week, trade the lists, and turn each list into a tiny improvised story.
Pick one room each and make a three-change comfort makeover using only objects you already own.
End the call by planning one small act of care each person can complete before your next long-distance date.
